abstract: Ultra-low-latency message pipelines require strict ordering guarantees and bounded propagation costs to support real-time perception systems. This work presents LowLatencyOrderPipeline, a pure TypeScript stream processing framework that enforces deterministic synchronous event propagation over a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Unlike asynchronous or lock-free concurrent queue implementations, LowLatencyOrderPipeline eliminates race conditions by design through synchronous execution and compile-time topology validation. We formally define the state transition semantics of the graph orchestrator and prove that cycle detection at connection time preserves the acyclic invariant, ensuring termination of all event traversals. We derive the asymptotic complexity of event propagation as $O(V + E)$, where $V$ is the number of visited nodes and $E$ is the number of traversed edges. Static Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis confirms the structural integrity of the implementation, verifying 199 lines of code and 11 function blocks with no external dependencies. This investigation addresses three research questions regarding structural bounds, invariant preservation, and static profile dynamics. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/typescript-design-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_084925_ultra_low_latency_ring_pipeline}.
